headline_marked: [[OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra]] autonomously completes Portal in 24 hours for $571
headline: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra autonomously completes Portal in 24 hours for $571
summary: The AI mapped game spaces, understood puzzles, and planned solutions, marking a significant step in multimodal AI intelligence.
details: An AI enthusiast has demonstrated OpenAI's new GPT-6 Astra model playing through Valve's Portal 3D puzzle game entirely on its own. This experiment showcases a remarkable advancement in multimodal AI intelligence, with the AI successfully mapping 3D game spaces and understanding complex puzzles before planning and executing solutions.

The autonomous playthrough involved 3,336 tool calls and incurred an API cost of $571.18. The enthusiast, CozyBlaze, clarified that these costs were covered by their $200 Codex Pro subscription. The AI controlled the game through a modified SourcePauseTool, receiving screenshots and player position data while the game was paused to plan its moves.

While the edited highlights reel of Astra's gameplay is approximately 2 hours long, the full duration of the AI's autonomous play, including thinking time, spanned about 24 hours. This achievement aligns with OpenAI's original 2016 technical goal of enabling a single agent to solve a wide variety of games.

CozyBlaze acknowledges that this runthrough is not a definitive AI benchmark and that many challenges remain. However, they view the general-purpose agent's autonomous navigation and completion of the game as a glimpse into that original vision becoming a reality. The code for CozyBlaze's Portal Agent is available on GitHub for those interested in exploring its inner workings.

headline_marked: Hikers [[ignoring safety rules]] get lost after trusting Google Gemini
headline: Hikers ignoring safety rules get lost after trusting Google Gemini
summary: Three novice hikers were rescued from Mount Shasta after relying on AI for trip planning, which advised insufficient food and water.
details: Three hikers were rescued from Mount Shasta after getting lost and spending a night on the mountain. They had used Google Gemini to plan their trip, but the AI reportedly advised them to pack inadequate food and water for the challenging ascent.

The hikers, described as 'novice,' set out at 3 am and reached the summit at 7 pm, well past the recommended turnaround time. This led to them hiking down in the dark, becoming disoriented, and eventually sheltering in a steep drainage with one hiker suffering a knee injury.

Local rangers and search-and-rescue volunteers were able to safely bring the group down. The sheriff's office emphasized the importance of proper preparation and having multiple, reliable methods of wayfinding, including offline options, rather than solely relying on AI.

This incident serves as a stark reminder that while AI can be a useful tool, it should not be the sole resource for critical planning, especially for activities with inherent risks like mountain hiking. Future AI-assisted adventures may not always end as fortunately.
